newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks hurdle 2400 level at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks hurdle 2400 level at open.

text.p: Australian shares hurdled the 2400 point barrier at the open on Thursday, the market trailing a record breaking Wall Street into uncharted territory.
From the opening, the All Ordinaries index climbed 13.5 points to 2,406.2.
The continuing Dow rally and base metals prices that looked to be holding the line sparked solid investor interest with the major miners and big banks again playing a starring role.
"It's got everything going for it at the moment," said Greg Matthews, executive director of Australian equities at Mercantile Mutual Investment Management.
"We've had a huge rally in the bonds, a huge rally on international markets, some good results coming out from the banks and base metals prices that have been holding up quite nicely."
Matthews was confident of the advance continuing, noting that there remained plenty of investment funds that were as yet uncommitted to the market.
"There is all this liquidity on the sidelines. There is a huge cash buildup in managed funds and cash management trusts are at record levels," he said.
National Australia led the banks higher as traders awaited the full year profit result due later today.
In the miners, CRA and BHP remained strong while MIM shares attracted plenty of investor interest, topping turnover and adding three percent in early trade.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about 13 to seven, while about 38 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
